The correct answer is: Option A i.e. J.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 people around a circular table, facing the centre.

 

• Only three sit between D and L (counting from the right of L); only three sit between K and I (counting from the left of K); B is immediately right of D; J is an immediate neighbour of both L and I.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Fix L at position 1 (clockwise numbering 1–7). 'Only three between D and L, counted from the right of L' places D exactly 4 seats clockwise from L: D = 5.

 

• 'B sits to the immediate right of D' gives B = 6 (clockwise neighbour of D).

 

• 'J is an immediate neighbour of both L and I' means J is sandwiched directly between L and I. Since L = 1, J must be at position 2 or 7; testing J = 7 forces I onto the already-used seat 6 (a contradiction), so J = 2, which makes I = 3 (J's other neighbour).

 

• 'Only three between K and I, counted from the left of K' places I exactly 4 seats anticlockwise from K, i.e. K = I + 4 = 3 + 4 = 7.

 

• The one remaining seat, position 4, goes to C.

 

• Final clockwise order: L(1), J(2), I(3), C(4), D(5), B(6), K(7) — and this satisfies every clue (verified by re-checking each one against this seating).

 

• 'Second to the left of C (position 4)': moving anticlockwise, 1st seat to the left is position 3 (I), and the 2nd seat to the left is position 2, which is J.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In circular arrangements, convert every 'counted from the right/left of X' clue into a fixed clockwise/anticlockwise seat-gap immediately, and place the person who is a 'common neighbour' of two others (like J here) as early as possible — it usually locks most of the remaining arrangement.

 

NOTE

 

• Always double-check whether 'left' and 'right' in a circular seating question are being asked from the point of view of a person facing the centre (directions reversed from an outsider's view) or facing outward — the question specifies facing the centre here.

question:
Select the triad that follows the same pattern as the one followed by the two triads given below. Both triads follow the same pattern.

 

OH-QK-TV

LE-NH-QS
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. RK-TN-WY.

 

GIVEN

 

• Two given triads: OH-QK-TV and LE-NH-QS, both following the same pattern.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 1st letters of OH-QK-TV: O(15), Q(17), T(20) → shifts +2, +3.

 

• 2nd letters of OH-QK-TV: H(8), K(11), V(22) → shifts +3, +11.

 

• Verify with LE-NH-QS: 1st letters L(12), N(14), Q(17) → shifts +2, +3 ✓; 2nd letters E(5), H(8), S(19) → shifts +3, +11 ✓.

 

• Now test option C, RK-TN-WY: 1st letters R(18), T(20), W(23) → shifts +2, +3 ✓; 2nd letters K(11), N(14), Y(25) → shifts +3, +11 ✓.

 

• Both column-patterns match exactly, so RK-TN-WY follows the same pattern.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Split each triad into its 'first letters' and 'second letters' columns and find the shift pattern in each column separately using both given triads before testing the answer options — this quickly eliminates options that get even one column's shift wrong.

 

NOTE

 

• A close-looking wrong option often matches the pattern in one column but fails in the other (e.g. matching the first letters but not the second) — always verify both columns before finalising.

question: Seven people, A, B, C, D, E, F and G, are sitting in a row, facing north. Only A sits to the left of D. Only four people sit between A and C. Only B sits between G and F and G is not an immediate neighbour of C. How many people sit to the right of G?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 4.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 people A–G in a row, facing north.

 

• Only A sits to the left of D; only four sit between A and C; only B sits between G and F; G is not an immediate neighbour of C.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'Only A sits to the left of D' means D is at position 2 (only one seat, A, to its left), so A = 1.

 

• 'Only four people sit between A and C' places C at position 1+4+1 = position 6.

 

• 'Only B sits between G and F' means G, B, F occupy three consecutive positions in order (G-B-F or F-B-G). Remaining open positions are 3, 4, 5, 7.

 

• The only run of three consecutive open positions is (3,4,5). So {G,B,F} occupy 3,4,5 in some order (as G-B-F or F-B-G), and E takes the leftover position 7.

 

• 'G is not an immediate neighbour of C (position 6)' rules out G sitting at position 5 (adjacent to C) — so the order F-B-G (which would put G at 5) is invalid, and the correct order is G(3), B(4), F(5).

 

• Final order (left to right): A(1), D(2), G(3), B(4), F(5), C(6), E(7).

 

• People to the right of G (position 3) are at positions 4, 5, 6, 7 → B, F, C, E = 4 people.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• When a clue gives a block of three people in a fixed relative order ('only B sits between G and F'), first find the only stretch of consecutive empty seats that can hold all three, then use any 'not an immediate neighbour' clue to pick the correct orientation of the block.

 

NOTE

 

• Always recount 'how many sit to the right of X' directly from the final fixed arrangement rather than from an intermediate one — an early placement can shift once later clues are applied.

question: Seven boxes, M, N,O, P, Q, R and S, are kept one over the other but not necessarily in the same order. Only three boxes are kept above S. Only one box is kept between R and S. Only three boxes are kept between R and Q. Q is kept at some place above S. N is kept immediately below Q. M is kept at one of the places above O. P is not kept immediately above or below R. Which box is kept at the lowermost position?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. O.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 boxes M–S, stacked, positions 1 (bottom) to 7 (top).

 

• Only three above S; only one between R and S; only three between R and Q; Q above S; N immediately below Q; M above O; P not immediately above/below R.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'Only three boxes above S' places S at position 4.

 

• 'Only one box between R and S' and 'Q above S, with only three boxes between R and Q' — testing R at position 2 (one box, position 3, between R and S at 4): then Q must be at position 2+4=6, which is above S — consistent, so R = 2, Q = 6.

 

• 'N immediately below Q' gives N = 5.

 

• Remaining positions 1, 3, 7 are left for M, O, P. 'P is not immediately above/below R (position 2)' rules out P at 1 or 3, so P = 7.

 

• M and O take positions 1 and 3; 'M is above O' means O = 1, M = 3.

 

• Final stack (bottom→top): O(1), R(2), M(3), S(4), N(5), Q(6), P(7).

 

• The lowermost position (1) is occupied by O.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• This puzzle mirrors the structure of a similar box-stacking question seen elsewhere in the paper — once S's fixed position is found from the 'boxes above' clue, chase each 'X boxes between' clue to an exact position the same way, rather than treating it as vague relative ordering.

 

NOTE

 

• When two positions satisfy an 'only one box between' clue, use the next constraint (like a further 'between' clue tied to a fixed anchor) to eliminate the invalid one, exactly as with R here.

question: Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-clusters are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which letter-cluster DOES NOT belong to that group? (Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter-cluster.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. MQL.

 

GIVEN

 

• Four letter-clusters: ORN, VYU, MQL, DGC.

 

SOLUTION (check the letter-position gaps within each cluster)

 

• ORN: O(15)→R(18) = +3; R(18)→N(14) = −4. Pattern: +3, −4.

 

• VYU: V(22)→Y(25) = +3; Y(25)→U(21) = −4. Pattern: +3, −4 ✓ (matches ORN).

 

• DGC: D(4)→G(7) = +3; G(7)→C(3) = −4. Pattern: +3, −4 ✓ (matches ORN, VYU).

 

• MQL: M(13)→Q(17) = +4; Q(17)→L(12) = −5. Pattern: +4, −5 — this does NOT match the (+3, −4) pattern of the other three.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For 3-letter clusters, compute the gap between the 1st–2nd letters and 2nd–3rd letters for all four options side by side; the pattern shared by three of them jumps out quickly, and the mismatched one is the odd one out.

 

NOTE

 

• Always compute gaps using actual alphabet positions (A=1 ... Z=26), not by 'eyeballing' letter distances — small counting slips are easy to make otherwise.

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series?

 

501 500 497 492 485 ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 476.

 

GIVEN

 

• 501, 500, 497, 492, 485, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Find successive differences: 500−501=−1; 497−500=−3; 492−497=−5; 485−492=−7.

 

• The differences themselves follow a pattern: −1, −3, −5, −7 — i.e. successive odd numbers being subtracted, increasing by 2 each time.

 

• Next difference = −9, so the next term = 485 − 9 = 476.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever a series' first differences themselves form a simple arithmetic pattern (here, consecutive odd numbers 1,3,5,7,9...), just extend that inner pattern by one more step and apply it to the last term.

 

NOTE

 

• Always verify the difference pattern using at least three consecutive gaps before trusting it, since two matching differences alone could be a coincidence.

question:
If 'A' stands for '÷', 'B' stands for '×', 'C' stands for '+' and 'D' stands for '−', what will come in place of the question mark '?' in the following equation?

 

24 A 4 B 6 C 2 D 10 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 28.

 

GIVEN

 

• A = ÷, B = ×, C = +, D = −.

 

• Equation: 24 A 4 B 6 C 2 D 10 = ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Substitute the symbols: 24 ÷ 4 × 6 + 2 − 10 = ?

 

• Apply VBODMAS (÷/× before +/−, left to right): 24 ÷ 4 = 6; 6 × 6 = 36.

 

• Now: 36 + 2 − 10 = 38 − 10 = 28.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Fully rewrite the expression with the actual symbols substituted before doing any arithmetic — this prevents mixing up which operation belongs to which letter mid-calculation.

 

NOTE

 

• Division and multiplication are evaluated strictly left to right when both appear consecutively (24÷4×6 is (24÷4)×6=36, not 24÷(4×6)).

question:
Refer to the following number series and answer the question that follows (all numbers are single-digit numbers only). (Counting to be done from left to right only).

 

(Left) 4 1 1 7 2 4 1 2 7 4 4 9 6 3 9 1 6 1 9 2 2 8 8 (Right)

 

How many such odd numbers are there, each of which is immediately preceded by an odd number and also immediately followed by an odd number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. Two.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 4 1 1 7 2 4 1 2 7 4 4 9 6 3 9 1 6 1 9 2 2 8 8 (positions 1 to 23).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Scan positions 2–22 and check: is the digit itself odd, is its previous digit odd, and is its next digit odd?

 

• Position 3 (value 1): previous = 1 (odd) ✓, value = 1 (odd) ✓, next = 7 (odd) ✓ — counts.

 

• Position 15 (value 9): previous = 3 (odd) ✓, value = 9 (odd) ✓, next = 1 (odd) ✓ — counts.

 

• No other position satisfies all three conditions simultaneously on careful re-checking.

 

• Total = Two.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• First mark only the odd-valued digits in the sequence (ignore even ones completely), then check just those marked positions for odd neighbours on both sides — this immediately halves the number of positions you need to inspect.

 

NOTE

 

• Re-verify each qualifying position by rewriting the small local triplet (previous, current, next) — it's easy to miscount positions in a long single-digit string.

question: In a certain code language, 'TOUR' is coded as '8571' and 'DOUT' is coded as '5478'. What is the code for 'D' in the given code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 4.

 

GIVEN

 

• TOUR → 8571; DOUT → 5478.

 

SOLUTION (rank the letters of each word alphabetically, and match to the code digits sorted in ascending order)

 

• TOUR: letters {T,O,U,R} in alphabetical order → O, R, T, U (ranks 1–4). Code digits {8,5,7,1} sorted ascending → 1, 5, 7, 8 (ranks 1–4).

 

• Matching ranks: O→1, R→5, T→7, U→8.

 

• DOUT: letters {D,O,U,T} in alphabetical order → D, O, T, U (ranks 1–4). Code digits {5,4,7,8} sorted ascending → 4, 5, 7, 8 (ranks 1–4).

 

• Matching ranks: D→4, O→5, T→7, U→8.

 

• Check consistency: T=7 and U=8 match in both words (they are always the two alphabetically largest letters in their set), confirming the method is correctly applied.

 

• So the code for D = 4.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In these letter-to-digit puzzles, if direct position-by-position matching doesn't stay consistent across both words, try ranking each word's letters alphabetically and pairing that rank with the code's digits sorted in ascending order — letters that are always the extreme (largest/smallest) in their word will validate the method quickly.

 

NOTE

 

• A letter's code can depend on its rank relative to the other letters in that specific word, not on a single universal fixed alphabet-to-digit key — always test consistency with a repeated letter (like T and U here) before trusting a derived mapping.

question:
What will come in the place of '?' in the following equation, if '+' and ' ÷ ' are interchanged and ' - ' and ' x ' are interchanged?

 

423 + 9 x 19 - 6 ÷ 775 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 708.

 

GIVEN

 

• '+' and '÷' are interchanged; '−' and '×' are interchanged.

 

• Equation (before interchange): 423 + 9 x 19 - 6 ÷ 775 = ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• After interchanging, '+' becomes '÷', '÷' becomes '+', '−' becomes '×', and '×' becomes '−'.

 

• The equation becomes: 423 ÷ 9 − 19 × 6 + 775 = ?

 

• Apply VBODMAS: 423 ÷ 9 = 47; 19 × 6 = 114.

 

• Now: 47 − 114 + 775 = −67 + 775 = 708.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Rewrite the entire equation with the new (interchanged) symbols first, in one pass, before calculating — trying to swap operators 'on the fly' while solving is where most errors creep in.

 

NOTE

 

• Double-check that both interchange pairs are applied correctly (+ ↔ ÷ is one pair, − ↔ × is a separate pair) — mixing the two pairs up is a common trap.

question: Mr. Akai starts from Point A and drives 11 km towards east. He then takes a right turn, drives 5 km, turns right and drives 14 km. He then takes a right turn and drives 16 km. He takes a final right turn, drives 3 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point A again? (All turns are 90 degrees turns only unless specified)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 11 km to the south.

 

GIVEN

 

• Start at A. Drives: 11 km east → right turn, 5 km → right turn, 14 km → right turn, 16 km → right turn, 3 km, stops at P.

 

SOLUTION (track coordinates, taking east as +x and north as +y; start at A = (0,0))

 

• 11 km east: position = (11, 0). Facing east.

 

• Right turn from east → south; drive 5 km south: (11, −5).

 

• Right turn from south → west; drive 14 km west: (11−14, −5) = (−3, −5).

 

• Right turn from west → north; drive 16 km north: (−3, −5+16) = (−3, 11).

 

• Right turn from north → east; drive 3 km east: (−3+3, 11) = (0, 11). This is point P.

 

• P = (0, 11), A = (0, 0). Since P is directly north of A by 11 km, to go from P to A Mr. Akai must travel 11 km to the south.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Track only the net east-west and net north-south displacement as running totals while reading through the turns once — the final direction back to the start is simply the reverse of the net displacement vector.

 

NOTE

 

• Since all turns here are 90°, each successive direction cycles predictably (east→south→west→north→east on repeated right turns) — writing this cycle down first avoids direction mix-ups.

question:
Which of the following letter-number clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete?

PDG 12, RFI 16, THK 20, VJM 24, ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. XLO 28.

 

GIVEN

 

• PDG 12, RFI 16, THK 20, VJM 24, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• 1st letters: P(16), R(18), T(20), V(22), ? — each step +2 → 22+2 = 24 = X.

 

• 2nd letters: D(4), F(6), H(8), J(10), ? — each step +2 → 10+2 = 12 = L.

 

• 3rd letters: G(7), I(9), K(11), M(13), ? — each step +2 → 13+2 = 15 = O.

 

• Numbers: 12, 16, 20, 24, ? — each step +4 → 24+4 = 28.

 

• Combining: XLO 28.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Handle the three letter-columns and the number column completely independently; each here increases by a fixed constant (+2 for every letter column, +4 for the number), so the next cluster can be written directly without re-deriving the pattern from scratch.

 

NOTE

 

• Cross-check that the letter shift (+2) is the same for all three letter positions — when a series looks 'too easy', it usually is exactly this simple, uniform-shift pattern.

question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

 

Statements:

Some keyboards are mouses.

All inverters are mouses.

 

Conclusions:

(I) Some keyboards are inverters.

(II) All mouses are inverters.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follows.

 

GIVEN

 

• Statement 1: Some keyboards are mouses (I-type statement).

 

• Statement 2: All inverters are mouses (A-type statement).

 

SOLUTION (Venn diagram / syllogism rules)

 

• Both statements share the common term 'mouses', but neither statement says anything that directly connects 'keyboards' and 'inverters' — both are only independently linked to 'mouses' (one partially, one fully), which is not enough to conclude a relationship between them.

 

• Conclusion I ('Some keyboards are inverters'): Cannot be concluded — the keyboards that are mouses and the inverters that are mouses need not overlap at all within the 'mouses' circle; two 'some'/'all-into-same-set' statements sharing a middle term don't guarantee this.

 

• Conclusion II ('All mouses are inverters'): Cannot be concluded — Statement 2 only tells us all inverters are mouses (inverters ⊆ mouses), not the reverse; there could easily be mouses that are not inverters.

 

• Since neither conclusion is forced to be true in every possible Venn diagram consistent with the statements, neither follows.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• When two statements only connect to a common middle term without directly relating the two end terms (keyboards and inverters here), draw the 'worst case' Venn diagram where the two end-term circles are drawn as far apart as possible within the shared circle — if the conclusion can be avoided in that diagram, it does not follow.

 

NOTE

 

• A very common trap is assuming 'All X are Z' and 'Some Y are Z' forces some overlap between X and Y — it does not, unless a direct statement links X and Y.

question:
Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-clusters are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which letter-cluster DOES NOT belong to that group?

(Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter-cluster.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. QPL.

 

GIVEN

 

• Four letter-clusters: QPL, AYV, BZW, DBY.

 

SOLUTION (check the letter-position gaps, allowing backward wrap-around)

 

• AYV: A(1)→Y(25) is 2 steps backward (A→Z→Y), i.e. −2; Y(25)→V(22) is 3 steps backward (Y→X→W→V), i.e. −3. Pattern: −2, −3.

 

• BZW: B(2)→Z(26) is 2 steps backward (B→A→Z), i.e. −2; Z(26)→W(23) is 3 steps backward, i.e. −3. Pattern: −2, −3 ✓ (matches AYV).

 

• DBY: D(4)→B(2) is 2 steps backward, i.e. −2; B(2)→Y(25) is 3 steps backward (B→A→Z→Y), i.e. −3. Pattern: −2, −3 ✓ (matches AYV, BZW).

 

• QPL: Q(17)→P(16) is 1 step backward, i.e. −1; P(16)→L(12) is 4 steps backward, i.e. −4. Pattern: −1, −4 — does NOT match the (−2, −3) pattern of the other three.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• When letter gaps look large or 'wrap past Z/before A', try measuring the shift in the backward direction too (cyclically) — patterns like −2,−3 are easy to miss if you only measure forward gaps.

 

NOTE

 

• Always test the pattern against all three 'normal-looking' options before concluding which is odd — here three different clusters shared the same hidden backward-shift pattern.

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series?

33 49 65 81 97 ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 113.

 

GIVEN

 

• 33, 49, 65, 81, 97, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Find successive differences: 49−33=16; 65−49=16; 81−65=16; 97−81=16.

 

• The series increases by a constant 16 each time (a simple arithmetic progression).

 

• Next term = 97 + 16 = 113.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

• Check the very first difference (49−33=16); if a series is a plain arithmetic progression, that single difference is all you need to extend it to the next term instantly.

 

NOTE

 

• Confirm the constant difference using at least two or three gaps before extending — a series that only looks arithmetic for one step can sometimes hide a more complex pattern.

question:
This question is based on the five, three-digit numbers given below.

(Left) 826, 117, 681, 964, 529 (Right)

(Example- 697 – First digit = 6, second digit = 9 and third digit = 7)

NOTE - All operations to be done from left to right.

 

What will be the resultant if the third digit of the highest number is added to the second digit of the lowest number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 5.

 

GIVEN

 

• Numbers: 826, 117, 681, 964, 529.

 

SOLUTION

 

• The highest number among these is 964; its third digit is 4.

 

• The lowest number among these is 117; its second digit is 1.

 

• Resultant = 4 + 1 = 5.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Identify the highest and lowest numbers first by simple comparison, then pick out only the specific digit asked for from each — no need to analyse the digits of the other three numbers at all.

 

NOTE

 

• Digit positions are always counted first, second, third from the left, as clarified by the example in the question (697: first=6, second=9, third=7) — don't miscount from the right by mistake.

question: Harshit starts from Point A and drives 6 km towards the east. He then takes a right turn, drives 6 km, turns right and drives 12 km. He then takes a right turn and drives 11 km. He takes a final right turn, drives 6 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point A again? (All turns are 90-degree turns only unless specified.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 5 km to the South.

 

GIVEN

 

• Start at A. Drives: 6 km east → right turn, 6 km → right turn, 12 km → right turn, 11 km → right turn, 6 km, stops at P.

 

SOLUTION (east = +x, north = +y; A = (0,0))

 

• 6 km east: (6, 0). Facing east.

 

• Right turn (east→south); 6 km south: (6, −6).

 

• Right turn (south→west); 12 km west: (6−12, −6) = (−6, −6).

 

• Right turn (west→north); 11 km north: (−6, −6+11) = (−6, 5).

 

• Right turn (north→east); 6 km east: (−6+6, 5) = (0, 5). This is point P.

 

• P = (0, 5), A = (0, 0). Since P is 5 km directly north of A, to go from P to A, Harshit must travel 5 km to the south.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Track only the running net north-south and net east-west totals as you read through the turns — for a closed rectangular-turn path like this, the final leg back to start is just the reverse of the net displacement.

 

NOTE

 

• On repeated right turns, direction cycles as east→south→west→north→east — writing this cycle out prevents direction errors over multiple turns.

question:
Refer to the following number series and answer the question that follows. Counting to be done from left to right only. (All numbers are single-digit numbers only.)

 

(Left) 4 6 5 8 2 2 1 8 2 9 8 4 7 4 8 2 4 3 1 4 1 2 7 2 6 (Right)

 

How many such digits are there each of which is immediately preceded by a perfect square and also immediately followed by a perfect square?

(NOTE: 1 is also a perfect square)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. Four.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 4 6 5 8 2 2 1 8 2 9 8 4 7 4 8 2 4 3 1 4 1 2 7 2 6 (positions 1 to 25).

 

• Perfect squares among single digits (given 1 counts): 1, 4, 9.

question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

 

Statements:

All schools are colleges.

No college is a radio.

 

Conclusions:

(I) Some colleges are schools.

(II) No school is a radio.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. Both conclusions (I) and (II) follow.

 

GIVEN

 

• Statement 1: All schools are colleges (A-type statement: schools ⊆ colleges).

 

• Statement 2: No college is a radio (E-type statement: colleges and radios are fully separate sets).

 

SOLUTION (syllogism rules)

 

• Conclusion I ('Some colleges are schools'): For any 'All A are B' (A-type) statement, its converse 'Some B are A' always follows, as long as set A is non-empty. Since all schools are colleges, some colleges are indeed schools. Follows.

 

• Conclusion II ('No school is a radio'): Since all schools are colleges, and no college is a radio, then no school (being entirely within the college set) can be a radio either — a valid chain (schools ⊆ colleges, and colleges ∩ radios = ∅ ⇒ schools ∩ radios = ∅). Follows.

 

• Both conclusions hold in every possible Venn diagram consistent with the two statements, so both follow.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Memorise two standard syllogism results: (1) 'All A are B' always converts to 'Some B are A'; (2) combining 'All A are B' with 'No B are C' always gives 'No A is C' — both apply directly here without needing to draw a full Venn diagram.

 

NOTE

 

• A chain of an A-type statement (All ... are ...) followed by an E-type statement (No ... is ...) reliably yields a valid E-type conclusion for the first and third terms — a pattern worth recognising instantly.

question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding to/subtracting from/multiplying with 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

 

(26, 46, 20)

(12, 16, 4)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. (9, 32, 23).

 

GIVEN

 

• Related sets: (26, 46, 20) and (12, 16, 4).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Test the relation: third number = second number − first number.

 

• (26, 46, 20): 46 − 26 = 20 ✓, matches the third number.

 

• (12, 16, 4): 16 − 12 = 4 ✓, matches the third number. Pattern confirmed: third = second − first.

 

• Check each option: (7, 23, 13): 23−7=16 ≠ 13. ✗

 

• (9, 32, 23): 32−9=23 ✓ — matches!

 

• (17, 43, 23): 43−17=26 ≠ 23. ✗

 

• (20, 31, 8): 31−20=11 ≠ 8. ✗

 

• Only (9, 32, 23) fits the pattern.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Once a simple relation (like third = second − first) is confirmed with both given sets, just apply that one subtraction to each answer option — no need to search for alternative, more complicated relationships.

 

NOTE

 

• The question explicitly disallows digit-breaking tricks — always test whole-number operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, ratios) between the three numbers first.

question: On 29 April 2025, the Union Minister of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) Pralhad Joshi launched the GHCI scheme to empower MSMEs and promote green hydrogen economy. What is the full form of GHCI?

question: In June 2025, which of the following announced to introduce 'Validated UPI Handles' effective from 1 October 2025 for secured payments by investors to enhance investor protection and combat fraud?

question: Which athlete received the Laureus World Sportswoman of the Year award in 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Simone Biles.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• American gymnast Simone Biles received the Laureus World Sportswoman of the Year award in 2025. (सिमोन बाइल्स — लॉरियस वर्ल्ड स्पोर्ट्सवुमन ऑफ द ईयर 2025)

 

• This recognition followed her outstanding performance at the Paris 2024 Olympics, where she won multiple medals, further cementing her legacy as one of the greatest gymnasts of all time.

 

• The Laureus World Sports Awards, often referred to as the 'Oscars of the sporting world', honour outstanding individual and team sporting achievements from the preceding year.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Simone Biles is the most decorated gymnast in World Championship history and has won numerous Olympic gold medals across the Rio 2016, Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024 Games.

 

• The Laureus World Sportsman of the Year award (the men's equivalent) has previously been won by legends such as Novak Djokovic and Lionel Messi in various years.

 

• The Laureus Sport for Good Foundation also runs the awards to promote the use of sport as a tool for social change.

 

NOTE

 

• Iga Świątek (Option A): A top-ranked tennis player and a past nominee/winner in different years, but not the 2025 recipient.

 

• Naomi Osaka (Option B): A former World Sportswoman of the Year winner in an earlier edition, not 2025.

 

• A'ja Wilson (Option D): A star WNBA basketball player, but not the 2025 Laureus Sportswoman of the Year.

question: In April 2025, Rapido signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Ministry of Labour and Employment to provide jobs through which of the following government portals?
solution_text:
The correct answer is National Career Service Portal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In April 2025, ride-hailing platform Rapido signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Ministry of Labour and Employment to list job/gig-work opportunities through the National Career Service (NCS) Portal. (रैपिडो — राष्ट्रीय करियर सेवा पोर्टल)

 

• The NCS Portal is a one-stop online platform that connects job seekers with employers, career counselling, skill development courses, apprenticeships and related career services across India.

 

• Such partnerships with gig-economy platforms are part of the government's push to formally integrate and track opportunities in India's rapidly growing gig and platform economy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• The National Career Service (NCS) initiative was launched by the Ministry of Labour and Employment in 2015 to transform the employment exchange system into a modern career-focused platform.

 

• The e-Shram portal is another key labour-ministry initiative, launched in 2021, to create a national database of unorganised and gig/platform workers.

 

• The Code on Social Security, 2020 was the first Indian labour law to formally define and extend certain social security benefits to gig and platform workers.

 

NOTE

 

• Startup India Portal (Option B): Supports registration and benefits for startups, run under the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), unrelated to this MoU.

 

• Digital India Portal (Option C): A broader digital-governance umbrella initiative, not the specific portal named in this MoU.

 

• Skill India Portal (Option D): Focuses on skill training and certification under the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, distinct from the National Career Service Portal named here.

question: The Indus Water Treaty, which was suspended by India following the Pahalgam terror attack in April 2025, was signed between India and Pakistan in ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1960.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) was signed between India and Pakistan in 1960, brokered by the World Bank. (सिंधु जल संधि — 1960)

 

• It was signed by then Indian Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and Pakistani President Ayub Khan, and governs the sharing of the waters of the Indus river system.

 

• Following the Pahalgam terror attack in April 2025, India announced that it was holding the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance (suspending it), marking a major shift in India-Pakistan relations over shared river-water management.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Under the treaty, India was given control over the three 'Eastern Rivers' — the Ravi, Beas and Sutlej — while Pakistan received control over the three 'Western Rivers' — the Indus, Jhelum and Chenab — though India retained certain rights (like limited irrigation, non-consumptive and hydropower use) even on the western rivers.

 

• The treaty had survived several India-Pakistan wars and periods of tension over more than six decades before this suspension, and is often cited internationally as an example of successful trans-boundary water-sharing diplomacy.

 

• The Permanent Indus Commission, with a commissioner from each country, was set up under the treaty to implement and manage its provisions.

 

NOTE

 

• 1950 (Option A), 1965 (Option B) and 1955 (Option C): None of these is the actual signing year — the Indus Waters Treaty was concluded in 1960, after nearly a decade of negotiations mediated by the World Bank.

question: Which summit in 2025 focused on 'securing our future' for Ukraine?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Warsaw NATO Ministers' Summit.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Warsaw NATO Ministers' Summit, held in 2025, was themed around 'securing our future' for Ukraine, focused on continued Western security support and long-term stability arrangements for Ukraine amid its ongoing conflict with Russia. (वारसॉ नाटो मंत्रिस्तरीय शिखर सम्मेलन)

 

• Discussions at such NATO ministerial meetings typically cover military assistance, reconstruction support, and Ukraine's long-term security guarantees in coordination with member and partner states.

 

• Poland, as a NATO member bordering both Ukraine and Belarus, has played a prominent role in coordinating Western support for Ukraine throughout the conflict.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• NATO's headquarters are in Brussels, Belgium, and its Secretary-General coordinates the alliance's collective response on matters like the Russia-Ukraine conflict.

 

• Various other international forums — including G7 summits and standalone peace conferences — have separately addressed different aspects of the Ukraine conflict since it began in February 2022.

 

• Volodymyr Zelenskyy has served as President of Ukraine since 2019, playing a central role in seeking international support throughout the conflict.

 

NOTE

 

• Kiev Peace Conference (Option A), London Summit on Ukraine (Option B) and Paris Peace Forum (Option C): These are plausible-sounding names of other Ukraine-related international gatherings, but the summit specifically themed 'securing our future' in 2025 was the Warsaw NATO Ministers' Summit.

question: How many positions did India drop in the 2025 Energy Transition Index compared to the previous year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 8.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India dropped 8 positions in the 2025 Energy Transition Index (ETI) compared to the previous year's ranking. (ऊर्जा संक्रमण सूचकांक 2025 — भारत की रैंक में गिरावट)

 

• The Energy Transition Index is published annually by the World Economic Forum (WEF) and evaluates countries on their readiness and performance in transitioning to secure, sustainable, affordable and inclusive energy systems.

 

• The drop in ranking, despite India's strong renewable-energy capacity growth, reflects challenges highlighted in the index such as energy security, affordability and equity aspects of the broader energy transition, relative to other countries' faster progress.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• The World Economic Forum (WEF), headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, is well known for publishing several global indices, including the Global Gender Gap Report, Global Competitiveness Report and the Energy Transition Index.

 

• India has separately been expanding its installed renewable energy capacity significantly, as part of its commitment to reach 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030, announced at COP26.

 

• Nordic countries such as Sweden, Denmark and Finland typically top such global energy transition rankings.

 

NOTE

 

• 6 (Option B), 5 (Option C) and 10 (Option D): These are close but incorrect figures — India's actual drop in the 2025 Energy Transition Index ranking was 8 positions.
